verses.1: At that time, King Herodes damaged the hands of those who were from the church.
verses.2: And Iacob, John’s brother, was killed by a sword.
verses.3: And seeing that it was pleasant for the Jews to have Petrus with them, as it was a day of celebration.
verses.4: And after you had taken him captive, you ordered that he be kept in prison. You assigned four soldiers to keep him there, with the intention of bringing him back to the people after the punishment was over.
verses.5: So, Peter remained in prison. However, the church prayed earnestly to the God for his sake.
verses.6: And as Herod was about to bring him forward, in the night, Peter was sleeping there, wrapped in a blanket between two soldiers. The guards stood guard at the door, keeping watch over the prison.
verses.7: And behold, an angel of the Lord appeared, and light was lit up in that house. He touched Peter’s shoulder and said, “Anastasius is coming soon.” Then, his gloves fell off from his hands.
verses.8: Then the angel said to him, “Live and multiply.” So he did. And the angel said to him again, “Cover your flesh with dust, and follow me.”
verses.9: And after he left, he continued to follow along. He didn’t know that what was happening was indeed true, due to the message sent by the angel. But eventually, he saw a sign.
verses.10: After passing through the first and second prisons, they arrived at the gate of the city. The gates were opened for them, and they entered the city. As soon as they stepped inside, the angel left him immediately.
verses.11: And Peter, becoming self-conscious, said, “Now I truly know that the Lord has sent his angel to me, and he has taken me away from the hands of Herod and from all the expectations of the people of Judah.”
verses.12: They gathered together and went to Maria’s house, the mother of John, who was also known as Mark. They were ready to gather together and pray.
verses.13: When he broke the door of the gate, a child named Rhodes came forward to stand guard.
verses.14: And knowing that Peter’s voice was not due to joy, she did not open the gate. Instead, she went ahead and told Peter to wait before entering.
verses.15: And those who spoke to her said, “May you be blessed.” But she refused to accept that. They said, “He is indeed an angel.”
verses.16: But Peter came forward, crying out. When they opened their doors, they saw him and rushed to greet him.
verses.17: Then, in a quiet voice, he told them how the Lord had brought him out of prison. He said, “Tell James and the brothers this.” After that, he went away to another place.
verses.18: It was indeed a chaotic day for the soldiers; hence, Peter came into being.
verses.19: Herodes, however, demanded that he be found and punished. He ordered the guards to search for him. After leaving Judea and heading towards Caesarea, he was captured.
verses.20: And they fought against the Tyrians and Sidonians. But they became allies with him. They convinced Blastus, who was on the throne of the king, to make peace with them, as a condition for allowing them to govern their own land from the royal domain.
verses.21: And one day, Herodes put on his royal clothes and sat down in front of them.
verses.22: And the crowd cries out: “The voice of God, and not of man.”
verses.23: But a messenger of the Lord came and ordered him to stop doing so, as he did not give glory to God. And when he became arrogant, he was punished.
verses.24: But God’s word became more widespread and popular.
verses.25: But Barnabas and Saul were allowed to go back to Jerusalem, after paying their taxes. They also brought with them John Mark, who had been called as a missionary.
